role.altitude: The analyst stops hand-building monthly Excel files and reconciliations. They own the HR metric layer: definitions of 90-day retention, verzuim rate and time to hire, the tests that guard them, access rules, and the verified answers that managers and Copilot query. They gain the right to block the release of a report or semantic model that fails its tests or lacks a definition.
reach: HR Administrator: correcting the AFAS data-quality exceptions the checks raise; learn which AFAS fields feed which metric so fixes go to the root.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: pay benchmarking against the CAO scales and the regional labour market; learn the CAO salary tables and shift allowances.
FP&A Analyst: headcount and flex cost forecasts per site; learn the agency-invoice and ledger side so HR and finance headcount match.
Controller: required filings and annual-report staff figures; learn the audit trail the controller needs before signing.
skills_to_grow: Writing automated data tests in SQL or Python that run after each AFAS refresh
Semantic model design for Copilot in Power BI: descriptions, synonyms, verified answers, row-level security
Writing bounded prompts with checks, and judging when no model step is needed
Privacy and works-council practice: AVG Art. 9 for absence data, WOR 27 consent files, DPIA basics
Explaining labour-market numbers to the HR director and site managers in plain language
role.ambitious_version: A tested HR metric layer on Power BI, with verified answers, that every site manager can query in Teams. Each monthly figure on retention, verzuim and flex use reconciles to AFAS and the agency invoices before anyone sees it. The analyst spends the freed time on one question a quarter that moves the North Star, for example why 90-day retention of order pickers in Venlo trails Tilburg. The works council consents to the whole setup once, not dashboard by dashboard.

tasks.short: Test that HR reports and metrics match what HR asked for and reconcile to AFAS.

steps.what: Agree the need and metric definition with the requester
Write test cases and expected values for each metric
Reconcile Power BI figures to AFAS after each refresh
Investigate failed tests and explain the difference

loop.input: failed test, the differing employee rows (pseudonymised ids), AFAS change log for those rows
loop.output: draft cause per break (late mutation, missing end date, definition gap) with row references
loop.check: every cited row must exist in the diff; cause must be one of a fixed list or 'unknown'
loop.stop: one pass per break, max 50 breaks per run; above that or on check failure, send the raw diff to the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: Rule checks catch known causes; the remaining breaks need reading of free-text mutation notes and context.

steps.what: Sign off the report with the requester

tasks.design: Replace the reconciliation spreadsheets with a scheduled test suite (SQL or Python) that runs after the nightly AFAS extract and before the Power BI refresh is published. Results feed a small test dashboard and a Teams message to the analyst; failed tests get a model-drafted cause list that the analyst checks and routes to the HR administrator for AFAS fixes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing and maintaining tests for every measure took more analyst time than checking by hand in Excel, and there was no data platform step between AFAS and Power BI to run them.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding writes the test code and expected values from a metric definition in hours; Power BI and Fabric dataflows allow a check step before publishing.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing one definition of 90-day retention or verzuim with HRBPs and finance; tests only guard what was defined.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the HR director actually means by a metric and spotting when a number is right but answers the wrong question.

ambition.what: Release the 90-day retention and verzuim figures to site managers daily instead of monthly, because each refresh is tested.

tasks.altitude: The analyst checks exceptions instead of rebuilding reconciliations, and gains the right to stop a release that fails its tests.

reach.task: Correcting AFAS records flagged by failed tests
reach.learn: Which AFAS mutations break which metric, so errors are fixed at entry.

evidence.claim: Automated data tests between a source extract and a BI refresh are standard practice.
Absence data is health data under GDPR Art. 9; tests and explanations must use rates and durations, never causes.
A tool that holds per-person rows can need works-council consent even if it shows totals.

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract lands in a place where a script can run before Power BI refresh.
About 40 to 80 HR measures are in active use.
unknowns: Whether Noordhaven has Fabric capacity or only Power BI Pro.
Whether written metric definitions exist today.
Whether the works council already consented to the Power BI HR dashboards.
research_questions: How many report errors reached managers in the last year, and what caused them?
How many hours a month does the analyst spend reconciling Power BI to AFAS?
Can the AFAS extract be checked before the Power BI refresh without new licences?

tasks.short: Analyse the regional labour market and competing employers' pay and offers for drivers and warehouse staff.

steps.what: Collect labour market data, CAO tables and competitor vacancy pay
Extract pay, hours and shift allowances from vacancy texts

loop.input: vacancy text from approved public sources
loop.output: structured row: role, site region, hourly pay range, hours, shift allowance, contract type
loop.check: schema check; pay within plausible bounds of the CAO scale; source link stored
loop.stop: one attempt plus one retry per vacancy; failures listed for manual entry
loop.why_not_simpler: Vacancy texts state pay in free and varied wording that rules do not parse reliably.

steps.what: Compare with own pay, offer acceptance and time to hire
Write interpretation and advice for HR director and C&B

loop.input: dashboard figures for the quarter and last quarter's brief
loop.output: draft brief with figures, changes and caveats
loop.check: every number in the draft must match a dashboard value; claims about cause must be marked as hypotheses
loop.stop: one draft, one revision; the analyst writes the advice section
loop.why_not_simpler: The summary needs prose; the advice stays with the analyst.

tasks.design: A quarterly Python job collects public labour market statistics and approved vacancy sources, a bounded extraction step turns vacancy texts into a pay benchmark table, and a Power BI page sets it against Noordhaven's CAO pay, offer acceptance and time to hire per site. A model drafts the quarterly brief from the dashboard; the analyst writes the advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competitor pay sits in unstructured vacancy texts; collecting and coding it by hand took days, so it was done rarely and on small samples.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap, checkable extraction of free text into fixed fields, and AI coding for the collection job and dashboard.
tasks.still_hard: Coverage and bias of vacancy samples, terms of use of job sites, and the fact that advertised pay is not paid pay.
tasks.human_edge: Judging what the market means for Noordhaven's offer to a Venlo reach-truck driver, and weighing it against CAO and budget.

ambition.what: Review entry pay and shift allowances per site each quarter before peak season instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The analyst moves from collecting data to advising the HR director and C&B on offers per site, with the brief as input to pay decisions.

reach.task: Setting pay above CAO minimum for hard-to-fill roles
reach.learn: How CAO scales, periodieken and allowances combine into the real offer.
Logging decline reasons in Recruitee consistently so they can be compared to the market.

evidence.claim: Models extract structured fields from free-text job ads with schema checks.
Market trend data does not show causes; keep caveats on cause.

assumptions: Market data contains no Noordhaven personal data, so works-council consent is light.
Recruitee holds decline reasons in a usable field.
unknowns: Which job sites and sources Noordhaven may legally use.
Whether staffing agencies share their hourly rates per role.
Whether decline reasons are recorded in Recruitee today.
research_questions: Does offer acceptance differ by site in a way pay could explain?
Do approved vacancy sources cover enough logistics employers near Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo?
Will the HR director change pay decisions more often given a quarterly brief?

tasks.short: Pull HR data from AFAS and agency portals and prepare required reports and filings.

steps.what: Export headcount, contracts, absence and pay from AFAS
Clean data and add flex workers from agency portals
Calculate the required figures per report
Write explanation and caveats for each report

loop.input: report figures, prior period figures, definitions
loop.output: draft explanation of changes with caveats
loop.check: all numbers match the figures table; no statement on absence causes or individuals; groups under 10 people suppressed
loop.stop: one draft and one revision, then the analyst edits
loop.why_not_simpler: A template fills the numbers; explaining changes in prose needs a model.

steps.what: Review with HR director or controller and submit

tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform pulls the AFAS extract and agency hours, runs fixed data-quality checks, and fills a template per required report (works-council social data, statistics surveys, annual-report staff figures, later pay-gap reporting). A bounded model step drafts the explanation; the analyst reviews, and the HR director or controller approves before anything leaves the company.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each report had its own Excel logic and flex workers sat in three agency portals, so the work was rebuilt by hand each cycle.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes per-report scripts and templates cheap to write and test; the nightly AFAS extract already exists.
tasks.still_hard: Changing legal definitions (for example pay transparency) and matching agency flex data to AFAS headcount.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding how to treat edge cases in a legal filing and answering for the figures to the controller, works council or authorities.

ambition.what: A quarterly works-council data pack on headcount, flex use and verzuim rates per site, produced from the same pipeline.

tasks.altitude: The analyst reviews and signs off filings instead of building them, and owns the definitions each filing uses.

reach.task: Staff figures in the annual report
reach.learn: The audit evidence the controller needs for headcount and personnel costs.
Which AFAS pay components count as pay under the EU pay transparency rules.

evidence.claim: Absence figures must be rates and durations, never causes; the AP fined a firm partly for recording sick-leave causes.
Absence data is special-category data under GDPR Art. 9.
Standard reports fit deterministic software plus a model-drafted narrative.

assumptions: Required reports number roughly five to ten recurring ones a year.
Agency portals allow a file export of hours per worker.
unknowns: The exact list of required reports and their deadlines.
Whether Noordhaven falls under CSRD and EU pay transparency reporting, and from when.
Whether the agency portals offer an API or only file exports.
research_questions: Which recurring reports take the most hours today, and how often are they corrected after submission?
Can agency hours be matched to AFAS sites and cost centres without manual mapping?
Does the controller accept script-produced figures with a test log as audit evidence?

tasks.short: Keep the library of metric definitions, report templates, DAX measures and queries current and findable.

steps.what: Spot or receive a new reusable asset or change
Write or update definition and how-to documentation

loop.input: measure name, DAX code, table descriptions, existing definition page
loop.output: plain-language definition, calculation, source fields, known caveats
loop.check: fields named must exist in the model; analyst approves before publishing
loop.stop: one draft per changed measure; unclear measures flagged for the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata can be listed by code, but a readable definition needs prose.

steps.what: Store and version templates, queries and report files
Find stale, duplicate or unused assets
Answer colleagues asking where a report is or what a metric means

tasks.design: Keep templates, queries and Power BI files in a versioned SharePoint library or Git, and run a monthly script that reads model metadata and usage to list undocumented, duplicate and unused measures. A bounded model step drafts definition pages that the analyst approves, and the same definitions feed Copilot in Power BI so colleagues get answers without asking the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documentation always lost to new report requests; nobody had time to write definitions or prune old files.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting definitions from DAX and metadata is cheap, and Copilot in Power BI uses model descriptions to answer questions.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping definitions agreed with HRBPs and finance; Copilot misreads poorly described models and Dutch questions are not officially supported.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which definition is the official one and retiring a report people still like.

ambition.what: Site and shift managers look up HR metric definitions and reports themselves in Teams for the first time.

tasks.altitude: Less time on filing and answering where-is questions; the analyst decides which definitions are official and which assets are retired.

reach.learn: Where HR and finance definitions of FTE and headcount differ, and agree one.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI answers questions on a semantic model but can misinterpret data without a prepared model; non-English chat is not officially supported.
Chatbots must disclose they are AI.

assumptions: The library holds metadata and definitions, not personal data.
Noordhaven has or will buy Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity for Copilot.
unknowns: How many reports and measures exist and how many are used.
Whether Power BI usage metrics are switched on.
Whether Fabric or Premium capacity is licensed.
research_questions: What share of questions to the analyst are about where a report is or what a metric means?
How many published HR measures have no written definition today?
Do Dutch-speaking managers get correct Copilot answers on a well-described model in a two-week trial?
